expected.statement: Let $j\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]) and let $g\colon U'\to U$ be a morphism of $S$-schemes. Then $j'\colon R'\to U'\times_SU'$ is an equivalence relation on $U'$ over $S$; if $g$ is etale, then $j'$ is an etale equivalence relation. expected.title: Representable morphisms of presheaves and fibrewise properties
expected.statement: Let $F$ and $G$ be presheaves of sets on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]) and let $a\colon F\to G$ be a morphism of presheaves ([[def-natural-transformation]]). For a morphism $\xi\colon T\to G$ from an $S$-scheme $T$ the fibre product $F\times_{G,\xi}T$ is the presheaf $T'\mapsto\{(x,\varphi):x\in F(T'),\ \varphi\colon T'\to T,\ a(x)=\xi\circ\varphi\}$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). We say $a$ is representable by schemes when for all $T,\xi$ this fibre product is representable by a scheme ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]], [[def-morphism-of-schemes]]). If $\mathcal P$ is a property of morphisms of schemes stable under base change, a representable morphism $a$ has property $\mathcal P$ when every base change to a scheme has $\mathcal P$; this defines representable etale, flat, surjective, open-immersion and closed-immersion morphisms ([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]], [[def-flat-morphism-schemes]], [[def-open-immersion-schemes]], [[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]). A representable morphism of sheaves is surjective when every section of $G$ lifts fppf-locally to $F$; an etale cover is a representable, etale, surjective morphism.
expected.strategy: Definition following Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Definition 65.3.1 and Definition 65.5.1 (tags 02W9, 025V), with the fibrewise convention of Stacks 65.5.2-65.5.4 and Vistoli Chapter 2. Representability and the property calculus are fibrewise: base change of a representable morphism along any morphism of presheaves is representable, and properties stable under base change pull back; composition is handled by the corresponding scheme lemmas. Surjectivity of a morphism of sheaves is the fppf-local lifting condition, which is equivalent to surjectivity of the induced morphism of sheaves (Stacks 65.5.5). No representability is asserted for arbitrary presheaf morphisms.

expected.title: The classifying stack of a finite group
expected.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the descent suppliers below. Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a finite group (for instance $G=\mathbb Z/2$), viewed as the constant group scheme $G_k$ over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]), acting trivially on $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $BG$ be the category fibred in groupoids over $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]], [[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]) whose fibre category over a $k$-scheme $T$ has as objects the right $G$-torsors over $T$ - fppf coverings $P\to T$ with a right $G$-action such that $G_k\times_kP\to P\times_TP$, $(g,p)\mapsto(pg,p)$, is an isomorphism - and as morphisms the isomorphisms of torsors. Then $BG$ is a stack in groupoids over $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]) and an algebraic stack over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-stack-and-inertia]]) with presentation $\operatorname{Spec}k\to BG$ given by the trivial torsor $G_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. For the trivial torsor $G_T$, the automorphism sheaf as a right $G$-torsor is $G_T$ by left multiplication. If $G$ is abelian, for every torsor $P$ over $T$ its automorphism sheaf is canonically $G_T$ by right translation, and the inertia stack satisfies $\mathcal I_{BG}\cong G_k\times_kBG$; over the trivial torsor in $BG(\operatorname{Spec}k)$ the inertia objects are the pairs (trivial torsor, $g$) with $g\in G$.

expected.title: Flat deformations of a smooth hypersurface are deformations of its equation
expected.strategy:
Proof. (1) Write $F=f+\eta$ with $\eta$ in the ideal $I\cdot(S\otimes_kA')$, $I^2=0$. If $F\cdot G=0$ in $A'[x]$ with $G\ne0$, reduce modulo the maximal ideal: $f\cdot\bar G=0$ in the domain $S$, so $\bar G=0$; then $G\in\mathfrak m A'[x]$ and induction down the $\mathfrak m$-adic filtration gives $G=0$. Hence $F$ is a nonzerodivisor, $A'[x]/(F)$ is flat over $A'$ (regular element over a flat algebra), and its zero scheme $Z(F)\subseteq\mathbb P^n_{A'}$ is flat over $A'$ with special fibre $Z(f)=X$; this is the elementary form of the local criterion of flatness ([[lem-flatness-affine-local-source-target]], [[def-flat-and-faithfully-flat-modules-and-ring-maps]]).
(2) On each affine chart $D_+(x_i)\cong\mathbb A^n_{A'}$ the subscheme $Y$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor of degree $d$: its ideal is invertible by flatness and the fact that the special fibre is a hypersurface (Nakayama for the finitely presented ideal, [[cor-nakayama-generators-modulo-an-ideal]]). Trivialize the ideal locally and dehomogenize: on the chart $D_+(x_i)$ choose a local equation $F_i$ of $Y$, so the local trivialization of the degree-$d$ twist is $F_i/x_i^d$. On an overlap the ratios $F_i/x_i^d$ and $F_j/x_j^d$ differ by a unit $u_{ij}$ congruent to $1$ modulo $I$, because both reduce to the same dehomogenization of $f$; the $u_{ij}$ form a Cech $1$-cocycle with values in the sheaf of units congruent to $1$ modulo the square-zero ideal $I\mathcal O$, which is additively $I\otimes_k\mathcal O$ and has $H^1=I\otimes_kH^1(\mathbb P^n_{A'},\mathcal O)=0$ because $H^1(\mathbb P^n,\mathcal O)=0$ for $n\ge2$ over any base ring ([[thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]]) and $I$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. Replacing the local equations by the units prescribed by a cobounding cochain makes the $(F_i/x_i^d)$ agree on all overlaps and glue to a global homogeneous form $F$ of degree $d$ with $Z(F)=Y$ on every chart, hence $Z(F)=Y$ in $\mathbb P^n_{A'}$. That $Y$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor follows because its ideal is finitely presented and flat over $A'$ with invertible special fibre, hence locally free of rank one by Nakayama ([[cor-nakayama-generators-modulo-an-ideal]]). Uniqueness up to a unit is clear because the ideal of a hypersurface in a chart determines the equation up to a unit, and these units glue. This is the standard chart computation of the embedded deformation functor (Hartshorne, *Lectures on Deformation Theory*, Chapter 1 Section 2 and Chapter 3 Section 21).
(3) Steps (1)-(2) give the claimed isomorphism of functors. The functor $R\mapsto\{F\equiv f\}/(R^\times)$ is the functor of points of the formal completion of $\mathbb P(S_d)$ at $[f]$, which is formally smooth since $\mathbb P(S_d)$ is a smooth $k$-scheme; hence all obstruction groups of the embedded deformation functor vanish. (4) The tangent space of that completion is the tangent space of $\mathbb P(S_d)$ at $[f]$, namely $\operatorname{Hom}(k f,S_d/k f)\cong(S/(f))_d$, and this is $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ by [[lem-cohomology-of-hypersurface-twists]](2); formal smoothness gives extension of first-order deformations. The dimension follows from $\dim_kS_d=\binom{n+d}{n}$.

expected.title: Tangent and obstruction spaces for hypersurface deformations
expected.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice (inherited from the projective-space cohomology suppliers, [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge2$, $d\ge1$, let $f\in S=k[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be homogeneous of degree $d$, let $X=Z(f)\subseteq\mathbb P^n_k$, and assume $X$ smooth over $k$ of pure dimension $n-1$. Then the embedded deformation functor of $X$ in the fixed $\mathbb P^n_k$ ([[def-embedded-deformations-of-a-closed-subscheme]]) has:
1. tangent space $H^0(X,\mathcal N_{X/\mathbb P^n})$ at the trivial deformation, and $\mathcal N_{X/\mathbb P^n}\cong\mathcal O_X(d)$, so the tangent space is
$$H^0(X,\mathcal N_{X/\mathbb P^n})\cong H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong(S/(f))_d,\qquad \dim_k=\binom{n+d}{n}-1;$$
2. vanishing obstruction space $H^1(X,\mathcal N_{X/\mathbb P^n})=H^1(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$, with the embedded deformation functor formally smooth and unobstructed: every embedded deformation over a small extension extends;
3. for the abstract deformation functor of $X$ as a $k$-scheme instead the tangent space is $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O_X}(L_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)\cong H^1(X,T_{X/k})$ and the obstruction group is $H^2(X,T_{X/k})$ ([[cor-deformation-cohomology-of-a-smooth-scheme]]); the two problems are related by the normal bundle sequence $0\to T_X\to i^*T_{\mathbb P^n}\to\mathcal N_{X/\mathbb P^n}\to0$ ([[thm-conormal-sequence-closed-immersion]]), which need not have vanishing maps, so the embedded and abstract deformation spaces are different in general.

expected.statement: Let $\Delta$ be the simplex category, with objects the finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]=\{0<\dots<n\}$ and morphisms the order-preserving maps. A simplicial object in a category $\mathcal C$ is a functor $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ ([[def-category]], [[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]); a simplicial set is a simplicial object in sets, a simplicial commutative ring is a simplicial object in commutative rings ([[def-commutative-ring]]), and a simplicial module over a simplicial ring is a simplicial object in modules with compatible action. Face and degeneracy maps are the images of the maps $[n-1]\to[n]$ that omit, respectively repeat, an index; they satisfy the usual simplicial identities. The Moore complex of a simplicial abelian group or module $M_\bullet$ is the chain complex with $M_n$ in degree $n$ and differential $d_n=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$ ([[def-chain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]]); its homology is written $\pi_n(M_\bullet)=H_n(M_\bullet)$ ([[def-homology-object-of-a-chain-complex]]). For a simplicial commutative ring $A_\bullet$ this defines $\pi_n(A_\bullet)$ for $n\ge0$, with $\pi_0(A_\bullet)$ a commutative ring and each $\pi_n(A_\bullet)$ a $\pi_0(A_\bullet)$-module. A morphism of simplicial rings is a weak equivalence when it induces isomorphisms on all $\pi_n$; the category of derived rings is the localization of simplicial commutative rings at weak equivalences ([[def-natural-transformation]]).
expected.strategy: Definitions with standard conventions, following Stacks, *Simplicial Methods*, Chapter 14 (simplex category 14.2, simplicial objects 14.3, homotopy groups 14.11-14.15, Dold-Kan 14.23-14.26) and Toen, *Derived algebraic geometry*, Sections 2.1-2.2. The identification of homotopy groups with homology of the Moore complex is the Dold-Kan normalization theorem; the local convention is to define $\pi_n$ by the Moore complex, which agrees with the classical definition (Dold-Kan; Stacks Section 14.24, Theorem 14.24.3, tag 019G). The ring and module structures on $\pi_*$ are immediate from the simplicial identities. No model-category machinery is introduced in the definition; weak equivalences are used only to state that later constructions are independent of choices up to canonical isomorphism.

expected.title: The standard simplicial resolution of a ring map
expected.statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings ([[def-ring-homomorphism]]) and for a set $S$ let $A[S]$ denote the polynomial $A$-algebra on $S$ ([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]). The standard resolution of $B$ over $A$ is the augmented simplicial $A$-algebra $\epsilon\colon P_\bullet\to B$ with $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, and in general $P_n=A[P_{n-1}]$; the face and degeneracy maps are induced by the counit $A[\;]\to\mathrm{id}$ and unit $\mathrm{id}\to A[\;]$ of the free-forgetful adjunction, and the augmentation $\epsilon$ is induced by the structure map $A[B]\to B$ ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]). Each $P_n$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra, and the augmentation is a weak equivalence of simplicial rings.
expected.strategy: The free-forgetful comonad unit and counit define the faces, degeneracies and augmentation, and their triangle identities give the simplicial identities. The augmentation's admissibility is now proved locally by [[lem-standard-polynomial-resolution-admissibility]], which supplies the explicit underlying extra-degeneracy contraction and the normalized abelian trivial-Kan criterion. This lemma is a justified_by supplier, since it depends on this definition. No unspecified model-category theorem is imported for this ordinary standard resolution.
